newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, October 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, October 10.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* It was a "black Wednesday" for the government as the majority was beaten in Parliament over a housebuilding decree-law (all).
* National Alliance leader Gianfranco Fini announces fierce opposition in Parliament to all measures linked to the 1997 budget (all).
* President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro says plans of an all-party bicameral commission to carry out constitutional reforms must go on. "I do not see any obstacles to such reforms" (all).
* Two former managers of the financial holding group Gemina have been arrested on charges of false accounting and three more are being sought (all).

* In an interview Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco says "The special tax for Europe will not hit industry" and adds "I can guarantee the 1997 budget will have no substantial impact on prices" so that interest rates can be cut (La Stampa).
* Fiat unions ask the government to intervene as the carmaker group announced temporary layoffs for November which forecast a production cut of 26,500 vehicles (all).
* Overall retail sales rose 0.5 percent in the second quarter of 1996 compared with the same period in 1995 (all).
* Enzo Berlanda, head of Consob, says Italy's stock market regulatory body is not worried by Olivetti's financial situation but will keep a close eye on developments (Sole 24 Ore).
* New Holland NV plans an Initial Public Offering in the US with the sale of 31 pct of its common shares, or $1,23 billion later this month (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
